q1: SELECT beer, MAX(price) - MIN(price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE beer IN (SELECT s.beer FROM serves AS s, frequents AS f WHERE s.bar = f.bar AND f.drinker LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2) GROUP BY beer ORDER BY beer
q2: SELECT b, (max_price - min_price), avg_price FROM (SELECT beer AS b, MAX(price) AS max_price, MIN(price) AS min_price, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE bar IN (SELECT bar FROM (SELECT bar, COUNT(*) AS servecount FROM serves WHERE bar IN (SELECT bar FROM frequents WHERE drinker LIKE 'B%') GROUP BY bar ORDER BY bar) AS barandcount WHERE servecount > 2) GROUP BY beer) AS beertable

explanation: Q1 filters beers served in at least 2 bars frequented by 'B%' drinkers, then computes price metrics. Q2 filters bars with more than 2 served beers (servecount > 2), then computes price metrics for beers served in those bars. A beer may meet Q1's criteria but not Q2's if its serving bars don't have servecount > 2.
